name: Coheed and Cambria
label: Equal Vision
lede: Coheed and Cambria started in Nyack, New York, with a breakup over gas money. Thirty years later it has told one science-fiction story across ten of its eleven albums, gone gold on a hardcore label, and outlasted a rhythm section's addiction, rehab and a pharmacy robbery.

eras.title: Gas money and a naked prey
eras.text: In Nyack, New York, Claudio Sanchez and Travis Stever cycled through band names like guitar strings. What stuck was Shabütie, a funk-punk-metal grab bag that slowly became the vehicle for a science-fiction story Sanchez was writing.

years.h: An argument over gas money ends Beautiful Loser
years.p: Sanchez and Stever had formed the band after Toxic Parents, with drummer Nate Kelley and bassist Jon Carleo. By June 1995 it was over, and Stever walked.

years.h: Shabütie takes its name from a chant in The Naked Prey
years.p: Sanchez, Kelley and Carleo borrow the name from the 1965 film and play everything from punk to funk to heavy metal under it.

years.h: A guitarist, [[Michael Todd|e0add4a2-5a48-4ed6-a52e-721074716c3f]], takes over Carleo's bass
years.p: Jon Carleo leaves Shabütie, and Todd, mainly a guitarist, is recruited to play bass.

years.h: Stever rejoins in time for The Penelope EP
years.p: That year Shabütie puts out the demo Plan to Take Over the World and the EP, and Travis Stever is back in the band.

years.h: Nate Kelley quits in the middle of a show
years.p: Kelley walks off during a live performance. Josh Eppard, drummer in his brother Joey Eppard's band 3, takes the kit.

years.h: Shabütie becomes Coheed and Cambria
years.p: The name comes from the husband-and-wife heroes of Sanchez's sci-fi story, and the Keywork becomes the logo. On the Delirium Trigger EP, Kelley drums but Eppard gets the credit.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the decision to rename to a 1998 trip to Paris. Several Delirium Trigger songs became the comic The Bag.On.Line Adventures, later retitled The Amory Wars.

The Keywork is the alignment of 78 worlds in that story.

years.h: The debut gets made at Stainglass Studio in Paramus
years.p: Michael Birnbaum and Chris Bittner produce The Second Stage Turbine Blade in October and November, the first of several records they'll make with the band.

eras.title: Gold on a hardcore label
eras.text: Equal Vision Records, Steve Reddy's label of Converge, Saves the Day and Krishna hardcore, released the first two chapters of the saga. The second went gold, and MTV played a band that sang about a sci-fi war as if it were a breakup record.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Second Stage Turbine Blade
yt: Devil in Jersey City, official video
years.h: The Second Stage Turbine Blade arrives on Equal Vision Records
years.p: Part one of the Amory Wars has [[Dr. Know|0fa99d3d-171f-462c-9620-31e41c2d9b85]] of [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] on guitar for Time Consumer. Old versions of Delirium Trigger and 33 still have Kelley on drums.
years.xp:
A hidden track, IRO-Bot, sits inside God Send Conspirator. Devil in Jersey City was the first single and video.

Critics were mixed to positive: AllMusic and Melodic.net gave it 3.5 stars each, antiMusic 4. Evil Ink put out a ten-issue comic adaptation in 2004, written by Sanchez and drawn by Wes Abbott.

years.h: Blaze James signs on as manager after a Warped Tour run
years.p: In summer 2002 the band also tours the U.S. and Japan, and does a brief stretch of the Vans Warped Tour. In August James becomes its manager.

years.src: Wikipedia: In Keeping Secrets of Silent Earth: 3
years.h: In Keeping Secrets of Silent Earth: 3 goes gold
years.p: Recorded at Applehead in Woodstock, New York, it reaches No. 52 on the Billboard 200 and No. 5 on the independent chart, and is certified gold by the RIAA.
years.xp: The record runs 69 minutes and ends with a hidden track, 21:13, after a run of silent tracks. Entertainment Weekly called it "one of the top five key albums in the new prog genre." Robert Christgau graded it a "(dud)."
play: In Keeping Secrets of Silent Earth: 3

years.src: Wikipedia: In Keeping Secrets of Silent Earth: 3
yt: A Favor House Atlantic, official video
years.h: A Favor House Atlantic gets onto MTV
years.p: Blood Red Summer follows in November. The band tours with [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]], [[Thrice|244afcb7-fa9a-49b1-9aa6-0149512d1c52]], [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]] and [[Rainer Maria|597dd959-1a24-457e-bea0-36f3fee2a5cb]], and wins two mtvU Woodies.
years.xp: The single came out June 8, 2004, and Blood Red Summer on November 9, both from In Keeping Secrets.

years.cap: Coheed and Cambria live in Central Park, New York
years.h: The cameras come to the Starland Ballroom
years.p: The band's August 2004 show in New Jersey becomes Live at the Starland Ballroom, its first live DVD, in March 2005.

eras.title: Columbia, rehab and a borrowed drummer
eras.text: Columbia signed the band and Good Apollo went top ten. Then the pressure cracked the rhythm section: Todd went to rehab, Eppard left before he could be fired, and the next album's drums were played by a Foo Fighter.

years.h: Columbia's first Coheed album peaks at No. 7
years.p: Good Apollo, Volume One sells almost a million copies, and critics heard Led Zeppelin's Kashmir in the riff of Welcome Home.
years.xp: It was the band's first major-label album, after a multi-album Columbia deal, and it pushed the sound from melodic post-hardcore toward full progressive rock. Tours with [[The Blood Brothers|b847568f-cd75-44c7-b87b-4f38a5a9f661]], [[Circa Survive|a2496a3c-8f42-4b98-b780-6f8d64f56441]], Dredg, Head Automatica and [[Avenged Sevenfold|24e1b53c-3085-4581-8472-0b0088d2508c]] followed, and Metal Hammer named it album of the year at its 2006 Golden Gods.
play: Good Apollo, I'm Burning Star IV, Volume One: From Fear Through the Eyes of Madness

years.h: Michael Todd leaves a European tour for rehab
years.p: He goes at the start of the 2006 tour with a growing heroin addiction, according to his Wikipedia entry, and Matt Williams covers on bass.

years.h: Sanchez steps out as The Prize Fighter Inferno
years.p: My Brother's Blood Machine is an acoustic-electronic prequel to the Coheed story. Sanchez said Coheed itself was first imagined as that kind of side project.

years.src: Wikipedia: Josh Eppard · Wikipedia: Coheed and Cambria
years.h: The band loses its drummer and its bassist
years.p: Josh Eppard, on whether he quit or was pushed. On November 2 the band announces his indefinite departure, with Michael Todd also gone.
years.xp:
Talk at the time was of creative limits. The cause, per Wikipedia, was Eppard's drug addiction, worsened by the frantic touring schedule. Matt Williams and drum tech Michael Petrak filled in on stage.

Eppard turned the experience into rap records as Weerd Science; his 2011 album Sick Kids looks at the addiction.

years.h: Todd is back for the Los Angeles sessions
years.p: Bassist Michael Todd returns as Coheed and Cambria start recording No World for Tomorrow with producer Nick Raskulinecz.

years.h: Chris Pennie joins, but Taylor Hawkins plays the album
years.p: Pennie leaves [[The Dillinger Escape Plan|1bc41dff-5397-4c53-bb50-469d2c277197]] for Coheed and Cambria, but contract restrictions keep him off the record. [[Taylor Hawkins|f0d35e7c-bbda-4063-a07b-0aa044fa5c8a]] of [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] drums instead, working from Pennie's ideas.

years.cap: Coheed and Cambria at Rock al Parque, Bogota, November 4, 2007
yt: Full set, Rock al Parque, Bogota, 2007
years.h: A fourth album closes the Amory Wars tetralogy
years.p: No World for Tomorrow reaches No. 6. The band headlines part of Warped Tour and opens a 25-city U.S. tour for [[Linkin Park|f59c5520-5f46-4d2c-b2c4-822eabf53419]].
years.xp: The Linkin Park tour forced the band to cancel its Soundwave Festival dates in Australia. The Feathers video, starring Rena Riffel, won Best Music Video at the 2008 Kerrang! Awards, and Welcome Home went into Rock Band that November.
play: Good Apollo, I'm Burning Star IV, Volume Two: No World for Tomorrow

eras.title: Four albums in four nights, and a bad night in Massachusetts
eras.text: The band played its whole catalog one album a night, wrote a prequel with a novel attached, and toured with Slipknot and Heaven & Hell. Then bassist Michael Todd was arrested at a gig for robbing a pharmacy, and the drum chair turned over again.

years.cap: Claudio Sanchez on the Kerrang Tour, April 2008
years.h: Neverender plays four cities, one album a night
years.p: New York, Chicago, Los Angeles and London each get one record per night, October to December. The box set Neverender: Children of the Fence Edition follows in March 2009.

years.h: Coheed and Cambria spends 2009 opening for Slipknot and Heaven & Hell
years.p: [[Slipknot|a466c2a2-6517-42fb-a160-1087c3bafd9f]] and Trivium take the early-year dates, Heaven & Hell comes in August, and the band plays Wacken, Sonisphere and Lollapalooza.

years.cap: Claudio Sanchez and Peter David at New York Comic Con, October 9, 2010
years.src: Wikipedia: In Keeping Secrets of Silent Earth: 3
years.h: A prequel album ships with a novel in the box
years.p: Year of the Black Rainbow jumps back to before the first record in the Amory Wars story. The deluxe edition's novel is by Sanchez and Peter David.
years.xp: David also co-wrote the comic adaptation of In Keeping Secrets with Sanchez, which began in May 2010.

years.h: Todd is arrested at the Comcast Center over a pharmacy robbery
years.p: On the Soundgarden tour at Mansfield, Massachusetts, Todd is charged with armed robbery of a Walgreens pharmacy in Attleboro and unlawful possession of narcotics.
years.xp: Wes Styles filled in for the rest of the tour, and on August 4 the band announced a mutual decision to part ways. On June 12, 2012, Todd pleaded guilty in superior court and was sentenced to one year of home confinement and three years of probation.

years.h: Five years after leaving, Josh Eppard is back
years.p: Chris Pennie leaves by mutual agreement over creative differences, and Eppard rejoins on drums.
years.xp: Eppard's return was announced November 16, 2011. He left Terrible Things, the rock supergroup he'd formed in 2009, at the same time.

eras.title: The lineup holds, the movie doesn't
eras.text: With Zach Cooper on bass and Eppard back, the lineup finally held. The band split one story across two albums, announced a Hollywood film that never got made, then stepped outside the Amory Wars for the first time.

years.h: A cold call from Blaze James lands Zach Cooper the bass
years.p: Cooper, of AM to AM, came on a personal recommendation. He's still in the band.

years.h: Hollywood announces a Mark Wahlberg film of the Amory Wars
years.p: At San Diego Comic-Con, producers Mark Wahlberg and Stephen Levinson say they'll develop a live-action film. Claudio Sanchez said in 2019 that Wahlberg's option had expired.

years.h: The Afterman: Ascension opens a double album
years.p: Recorded at Applehead in Woodstock. Sirius Amory finds that the Keywork's energy is an afterlife for departed souls.

years.h: The Afterman: Descension follows four months later
years.p: The second half of the double album arrives with videos for Dark Side of Me and Number City.

years.cap: Travis Stever at the Mercury Ballroom, October 6, 2014
years.h: In Keeping Secrets gets a remaster and a full-album tour
years.p: The gold second album is reissued, and the band takes it out with Thank You Scientist, playing it start to finish.

years.h: For once the story is Sanchez's own
years.p: The Color Before the Sun is the first album outside the Amory Wars. Sanchez writes about moving from the country to the city and the birth of his son Atlas in June 2014.

years.cap: Coheed and Cambria at Summer Breeze, Dinkelsbühl, August 19, 2016
years.h: [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]], I the Mighty and Silver Snakes ride along on the U.S. tour
years.p: Later tours bring [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]] and Polyphia.

eras.title: Back to the story, with Roadrunner
eras.text: A deal with Roadrunner Records brought the band back to the saga with a new five-part arc, Vaxis, and back to arenas with Mastodon. Three acts in, the story is still unfolding.

years.cap: Coheed and Cambria with the National Symphony Orchestra Pops at NASA's 60th anniversary concert, Washington, June 1, 2018
years.h: Roadrunner Records becomes the band's third label home
years.p: Coheed and Cambria started on Equal Vision, broke through on Columbia, and now hints at a return to the Amory Wars.

years.h: A new Amory Wars arc starts with Act I
years.p: Vaxis – Act I: The Unheavenly Creatures is the ninth album and the first part of a five-part arc.
play: Vaxis – Act I: The Unheavenly Creatures

years.h: Mastodon co-headlines the Unheavenly Skye Tour
years.p: [[Every Time I Die|ef90f210-f136-4386-ab37-8c00d04eeace]] opens, with Coheed and Cambria and [[Mastodon|bc5e2ad6-0a4a-4d90-b911-e9a7e6861727]] splitting the top billing.

years.h: Rick Springfield sings on the sequel to his own Jessie's Girl
years.p: Coheed and Cambria wrote Jessie's Girl 2, a follow-up to the 1981 hit. Entertainment Weekly reported they'd considered a whole album of sequels to other people's songs.

years.h: Act II arrives, with plot points rethought after COVID-19
years.p: Vaxis – Act II: A Window of the Waking Mind is the tenth album. Sanchez said some plot points felt insensitive after COVID-19 and needed rethinking.
years.xp: [[Alkaline Trio|69421e11-e4c3-4854-951b-ceab4972e38e]] replaced Dance Gavin Dance on the summer tour.
play: Vaxis – Act II: A Window of the Waking Mind

years.h: Album eleven arrives with the Infinite Arc Tour
years.p: Vaxis – Act III: The Father of Make Believe comes out March 14 and tours with Mastodon and Periphery. A deluxe New Entities Edition with four new tracks follows in October.
